issues.title: Malformed right-eigenvalue cardinality claim

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\sigma(A)$ be the set of all right eigenvalues of $A$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines sigma(A) as a set of right eigenvalues. For the admissible Hermitian matrix A=I_n with n>1, I_n z=z lambda forces lambda=1, so the set has cardinality one rather than n. Moreover, the matrix space Q^{n x n} itself is not the matrix whose eigenvalues are being counted. The valid statement needed later is that A has at most n distinct right eigenvalues, equivalently that it has n eigenvalues only when multiplicity is counted.
issues.overall_effect: The literal lemma does not provide the distinct-eigenvalue cardinality bound invoked for PCG finite termination and later reused in the superlinear-convergence proof, although those arguments need only the corrected local bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Lemma hpdqmatproplm(ii)'s malformed cardinality clause by: for Hermitian A, σ(A) is a subset of the reals and |σ(A)| ≤ n, equivalently A has n real eigenvalues when multiplicity is counted. Retain the HPD positivity clause and use this distinct-eigenvalue bound in qhpdpcgcvtthm and strangcircmainthm; no proof restructuring is needed.
issues.why_classification: The lemma's matrix A is the only possible object whose spectrum can be meant, σ(A) was explicitly defined as a set, and the later PCG proof expressly invokes |σ(A)| ≤ n. Thus the old source uniquely forces the standard corrected reading, and an adept reader can continue without repairing any inference or construction.

issues.title: Wrong upper-right sign in the matrix-valued symbol
issues.failure_explanation: Lemma gfuncstructurelm makes the diagonal entries real. With lower-left entry conjugate(phi_2(f)(x)), the conjugate-transpose condition forces the upper-right entry to be phi_2(f)(x). The old theorem instead defines it as -phi_2(f)(x), so G[f] is generally non-Hermitian when phi_2 is nonzero. Moreover, the theorem's own assembled quadratic-form matrix has the positive entry, making its final identification with the displayed G[f] false.
issues.overall_effect: The stated quadratic-form representation and the claim that G[f] is Hermitian fail as written, leaving the ensuing spectral bounds, HPD criterion, Szegő result, and preconditioned spectral chain unsupported until the sign is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change only the upper-right entry in the definition of G[f](x) from −φ₂(f)(x) to φ₂(f)(x), giving the Hermitian block [[φ₁(f)(x), φ₂(f)(x)], [conjugate(φ₂(f)(x)), φ₁(f)(−x)]], and use that corrected definition throughout the listed dependent results. The minus sign in the separate quaternion complexification map need not be changed.
issues.why_classification: The real diagonal entries and displayed lower-left entry uniquely force the positive upper-right entry, and the theorem's own assembled quadratic-form matrix already has that entry. This is a transcriptional sign error; correcting it makes the existing argument and dependent spectral formulas consistent without new mathematical work.

issues.title: Covariance-lag orientation in the predictor-system construction
issues.failure_explanation: The old convention is eta(k)=E(x(u) conjugate(x(u-k))). For s' greater than or equal to s, the normal-equation entry E(x(t-s') conjugate(x(t-s))) therefore equals conjugate(eta(s'-s)), whereas the printed construction assigns eta(s'-s). For s'<s the opposite branch is likewise reversed. The old right-hand side conjugate(eta(s')) is consistent with the backward convention, so it does not cure the matrix error. Non-real quaternion covariances, including those allowed by the paper's examples, expose the mismatch.
issues.overall_effect: For non-real lag covariances, the assembled Toeplitz system is not the normal-equation system for the stated prediction problem. Its generating function, examples, and sampling construction consequently use the wrong orientation, although the abstract Toeplitz theorems do not depend on this signal interpretation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the old backward-lag convention η(k)=E(x(u) conjugate(x(u−k))) and replace the predictor matrix entries by conjugate(η(s′−s)) for s′≥s and η(s−s′) for s′<s; the right-hand side remains [conjugate(η(1)),…,conjugate(η(n))]^T. Correspondingly use f(θ)=η(0)+Σ_{k≥1}[conjugate(η(k))exp(pkθ)+η(k)exp(−pkθ)] and make the same systematic orientation swap in the two examples and the sampled Toeplitz construction, including its factorization.
issues.why_classification: The adjacent normal equations determine the corrected conjugations by a short stationarity calculation. Although the same convention must be propagated through several signal-processing formulas, this is routine local bookkeeping that preserves the prediction objective, stochastic models, Toeplitz method, and all abstract spectral and convergence guarantees; it requires no new lemma, architecture, or reoptimization.

issues.title: Incorrect component symbols in the Strang-circulant proof
issues.failure_explanation: At theta_s=2 pi s/n, the first-column coefficients of c(-phi_2(T_n)) produce phi_2(f_m)(theta_s), not its negative. Entrywise conjugation of phi_1(T_n) reverses the Fourier frequency, so c(conjugate(phi_1(T_n))) has symbol phi_1(f_m)(-theta_s), not conjugate(phi_1(f_m)(theta_s)). Although phi_1(f_m) is real-valued, it need not be even. Thus the old diagonal 2-by-2 blocks are not the actual Fourier blocks and are generally non-Hermitian.
issues.overall_effect: Parts (i) and (ii) of the Strang-circulant lemma are not established by the old block diagonalization, so the later proof that the preconditioner is eventually HPD and the resulting clustering and superlinear-convergence chain lose this input.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the scalar-circulant Fourier symbols from their first columns: at θ_s=2πs/n, c(−φ₂(T_n)) contributes Φ₂[f_m](θ_s), while c(conjugate(φ₁(T_n))) contributes Φ₁[f_m](−θ_s). Replace the resulting 2-by-2 Fourier blocks by [[Φ₁[f_m](θ_s), Φ₂[f_m](θ_s)], [conjugate(Φ₂[f_m](θ_s)), Φ₁[f_m](−θ_s)]]. Then use the oddness of Φ₂ and either the corrected block similarity or the 2-by-2 characteristic polynomial to pair θ_s with −θ_s; the existing uniform-convergence argument proves part (ii), after which the two dependent theorems proceed unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old proof uses incorrect component symbols, so this is not merely typographical. Nevertheless, the repair is a short, local Fourier-frequency and conjugation calculation using machinery already present in the proof. It restores both parts of the lemma and the downstream HPD, clustering, and superlinear-convergence chain at full strength without a new lemma or proof architecture.

issues.title: Missing justification that quaternion PCG coefficients are real
issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines the inner product as y* x, which can be non-real; for scalar vectors x=1 and y=p it equals -p. Therefore the statement that PCG step parameters are inner products does not by itself imply that the coefficients zeta_s are real. Their reality is needed so that the polynomial coefficients commute and the real-spectral minimax argument transfers from complex PCG. It follows locally only after identifying forms such as r_k*P^{-1}r_k and p_k*A p_k and applying hpdqmatproplm(i).
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish the real-coefficient polynomial representation required for the PCG minimax estimate and finite-termination argument, and consequently does not support the later prepared estimate and superlinear-convergence theorem through this route.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the quaternion PCG recurrences explicitly enough to identify their scalar parameters as ratios of forms such as r_k*P^−1r_k and p_k*Ap_k. Since P^−1 and A are HPD, Lemma hpdqmatproplm(i) makes these forms positive real numbers, so all recurrence parameters and hence the expanded coefficients ζ_s are real and commute with the matrices. A short induction then gives the real-coefficient polynomial representation, allowing the standard minimax and finite-termination arguments and their two dependent results to remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The claim that arbitrary quaternion inner products are real is an invalid inference, so the issue is substantive rather than a typo. The missing fact is nevertheless supplied locally by the paper's HPD quadratic-form lemma and the standard PCG recurrence; only a short routine justification is needed, with no weakening of the error estimate, iteration bound, or superlinear-convergence guarantee.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: forms / inner products (e.g., ${\bf r}_k^*P^{-1}{\bf r}_k$ and ${\bf p}_k^*A{\bf p}_k$)
